answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a bond locked per agent identity until independent attesters confirm the identity did real work. The bond is a prism for cost: each identity mirrors a separate upfront lock. Attesters are drawn at random from a pool the attacker cannot predict, so a farm must also fake N attestation links, and any self-attested pair forfeits its bond. The attacker's price grows linearly while reward per identity stays capped, pushing margin negative early. An honest operator pays one lock and reaches the zenith of the registry cheaply, while farms climb toward no vertex at all.
